result.topic_en: Ramanujan derives, for a highly composite number N written as a product of primorial-type factors e^{\vartheta(p_1)+\vartheta(p_2)+\dots}, a lower bound on the divisor function and an inequality between Chebyshev theta-function values obtained by comparing N with a modified number N'.
result.transcription:
Add ms a 94 18 (54)    (54)
If $N = e^{\vartheta(\alpha)+\vartheta(\beta)+\vartheta(\gamma)+\cdots}$
then $d(N) \geqslant 2^{\pi(\alpha)}\left(\tfrac{3}{2}\right)^{\pi(\beta)}\left(\tfrac{4}{3}\right)^{\pi(\gamma)}\cdots\cdots$.
If $\alpha \geqslant \beta \geqslant \gamma \geqslant \cdots\cdots$ then only
$d(N) = 2^{\pi(\alpha)}\left(\tfrac{3}{2}\right)^{\pi(\beta)}\left(\tfrac{4}{3}\right)^{\pi(\gamma)}\cdots\cdots$
Let $N$ be highly composite such that
$N = e^{\vartheta(p_1)+\vartheta(p_2)+\vartheta(p_3)+\cdots\cdots}$
and $d(N) = 2^{\pi(p_1)}\left(\tfrac{3}{2}\right)^{\pi(p_2)}\left(\tfrac{4}{3}\right)^{\pi(p_3)}\cdots\cdots$,
Let $N' = N e^{\vartheta(q_r)+\vartheta(q_s)-\vartheta(p_r)-\vartheta(p_s)}$
Then $d(N') \geqslant d(N)\left(1+\tfrac{1}{r}\right)^{\pi(q_r)-\pi(p_r)}\left(1+\tfrac{1}{s}\right)^{\pi(q_s)-\pi(p_s)}$.
Let us suppose that
$q_r > p_r\,,\quad q_s < p_s\,,$
and
(1) $\begin{cases}\pi(q_r) = \pi(p_r) + n\,,\\ \pi(q_s) = \pi(p_s) - \left[\dfrac{n\log(1+\frac{1}{r})}{\log(1+\frac{1}{s})}\right].\end{cases}$
We have then
$d(N') \geqslant d(N)$
and so $N' \geqslant N$,
That is to say
$\vartheta(q_r)+\vartheta(q_s) \geqslant \vartheta(p_r)+\vartheta(p_s)$.
But if $\alpha > \beta$, then
$\{\pi(\alpha)-\pi(\beta)\}\log\alpha \geqslant \vartheta(\alpha)-\vartheta(\beta) \geqslant \{\pi(\alpha)-\pi(\beta)\}\log\beta$.
Hence

methods.what: Lower bound for the divisor function of a product of primorials expressed via Chebyshev's theta function
Equality condition for the divisor count when the parameters are decreasing
Comparison method: perturb a highly composite N to N' by exchanging primes and compare divisor counts
Choice of q_r, q_s so that d(N') >= d(N), giving an inequality on theta-function values since N is highly composite
Elementary bounds for differences of Chebyshev's theta function in terms of differences of pi
